name: Battle of Waterloo
note: Positions are schematic: the account gives the ground and the order of the corps, not exact places. The line is placed with Wellington's ridge at the top and the French below it, the Brussels road running between them, and the Prussians arriving from the east; the account does not name compass points. Other accounts give different times for the start of the fighting at Hougoumont.

terrain.name: Mont-Saint-Jean ridge
terrain.quote: It consisted of a long ridge running east–west, perpendicular to, and bisected by, the main road to Brussels.

terrain.name: Brussels road
terrain.quote: perpendicular to, and bisected by, the main road to Brussels

terrain.name: Hougoumont
terrain.quote: On the extreme right were the château, garden, and orchard of Hougoumont.

terrain.name: Papelotte
terrain.quote: On the extreme left was the hamlet of Papelotte.

terrain.name: La Haye Sainte
terrain.quote: was the farmhouse and orchard of La Haye Sainte, which was garrisoned with 400 light infantry of the King's German Legion

terrain.name: Plancenoit
terrain.quote: In the right rear of the French position was the substantial village of Plancenoit

units.name: Hougoumont garrison
units.quote: The house and its immediate environs were defended by four light companies of Guards

units.name: Anglo-allied centre
units.quote: Wellington deployed his infantry in a line just behind the crest of the ridge following the Ohain road.

units.name: Anglo-allied left
units.quote: the first line consisted of the 1st brigade (Van Bylandt's brigade) of the 2nd Netherlands Division, flanked by the British brigades of Kempt and Pack on either side

units.name: British heavy cavalry
units.quote: Uxbridge ordered his two brigades of British heavy cavalry—formed unseen behind the ridge—to charge

units.name: Prussian IV Corps
units.quote: The Prussian IV Corps (Bülow's) was the first to arrive in strength.

units.name: Prussian I Corps
units.quote: the Prussian I Corps (Zieten's) had been arriving in greater strength in the area just north of La Haie

units.name: French II Corps
units.quote: On the left was II Corps under Reille with 13,000 infantry, and 1,300 cavalry

units.name: French I Corps
units.quote: On the right was I Corps under d'Erlon with 16,000 infantry and 1,500 cavalry

units.name: Grande batterie
units.quote: The 80 guns of Napoleon's grande batterie drew up in the centre.

units.name: French reserve cavalry
units.quote: Initially, Milhaud's reserve cavalry corps of cuirassiers and Lefebvre-Desnoëttes' light cavalry division of the Imperial Guard, some 4,800 sabres, were committed.

units.name: Imperial Guard
units.quote: the 13,000 infantry of the Imperial Guard

units.name: French VI Corps
units.quote: a reserve including Lobau's VI Corps with 6,000 men

units.name: Rallied I Corps elements
units.quote: rallied elements of D'Erlon's I Corps, spearheaded by the 13th Légère

units.name: Young Guard
units.quote: Napoleon had dispatched all eight battalions of the Young Guard to reinforce Lobau

phases.title: The armies face each other across the Brussels road
phases.text: Wellington drew up his infantry just behind the crest of the ridge, with Hougoumont held ahead of his right and his heavy cavalry out of sight behind the ridge. The French formed on the slopes of another ridge to the south, symmetrically about the road.
phases.quote: The French army formed on the slopes of another ridge to the south.

phases.title: Hougoumont is attacked and the grande batterie fires
phases.text: Reille's corps pressed in on Hougoumont, which the Guards light companies and others held, and the fighting there lasted all afternoon. The 80 guns of the grande batterie fired on Wellington's centre.
phases.quote: Fighting continued around Hougoumont all afternoon.

phases.title: I Corps advances against Wellington's left
phases.text: D'Erlon advanced some 14,000 men against Wellington's left wing, where about 6,000 stood in the first line. His divisions reached the sunken Ohain road and pushed back Bylandt's brigade.
phases.quote: d'Erlon started to advance his three other divisions, some 14,000 men over a front of about 1,000 metres (1,100 yards), against Wellington's left wing

phases.title: The British heavy cavalry charge and I Corps breaks
phases.text: Uxbridge ordered his two heavy brigades, formed unseen behind the ridge, to charge. They crossed the crest and went downhill, and I Corps was driven back across the valley in rout.
phases.quote: The Household Brigade crossed the crest of the Anglo-allied position and charged downhill.

phases.title: Some of the cavalry ride on to the French guns
phases.text: The British horsemen lost their cohesion and found themselves before the main French lines, on blown horses. Some attacked the guns of the grande batterie and put many of them out of action.
phases.quote: Some attacked nearby gun batteries of the Grande Battery.

phases.title: The French cavalry counter-charge
phases.text: Napoleon ordered a counter-attack by cuirassiers and lancers. They caught the scattered British cavalry in the valley and drove the Union Brigade from it, with very heavy losses.
phases.quote: Milhaud's and Jaquinot's cavalrymen drove the Union Brigade from the valley.

phases.title: The French cavalry attack the centre
phases.text: Ney tried to break Wellington's centre with cavalry alone, sending in his reserve cavalry between Hougoumont and La Haye Sainte. Wellington's infantry formed squares against them.
phases.quote: Ney therefore tried to break Wellington's centre with cavalry alone.

phases.title: La Haye Sainte falls to the French
phases.text: Rallied elements of I Corps, led by the 13th Légère, renewed the attack on La Haye Sainte and took it once the German garrison's ammunition ran out. The French then brought skirmishers and guns up towards the centre.
phases.quote: renewed the attack on La Haye Sainte and this time were successful

phases.title: The Prussians arrive and Lobau is sent to stop them
phases.text: Bülow's IV Corps came up on the French right with Plancenoit as its objective. Napoleon sent Lobau's corps to stop it.
phases.quote: Napoleon sent Lobau's corps to stop the rest of Bülow's IV Corps proceeding to Plancenoit.

phases.title: The Young Guard fights for Plancenoit
phases.text: Napoleon sent the Young Guard to reinforce Lobau, who was hard pressed. It secured Plancenoit and was driven out, and two battalions of the Middle or Old Guard then recaptured the village.
phases.quote: The Young Guard counter-attacked and, after very hard fighting, secured Plancenoit, but were themselves counter-attacked and driven out.

phases.title: Zieten's I Corps attacks the French right
phases.text: Zieten's Prussian I Corps came up in strength north of La Haie and attacked the French troops before Papelotte. By 19:30 the French position was bent into a rough horseshoe.
phases.quote: I Corps proceeded to attack the French troops before Papelotte and by 19:30 the French position was bent into a rough horseshoe shape.

phases.title: The Imperial Guard attacks and I Corps breaks
phases.text: Napoleon committed the Imperial Guard against Wellington's centre, led by Ney. As it went forward the rest of d'Erlon's corps broke and fled.
phases.quote: This attack, mounted at around 19:30, was intended to break through Wellington's centre and roll up his line away from the Prussians.

phases.title: The Guard retreats and Wellington advances
phases.text: The Guard was repulsed and the last of it retreated. Wellington signalled a general advance and his army went forward against the retreating French.
phases.quote: Wellington now stood up in Copenhagen's stirrups and waved his hat in the air to signal a general advance. His army rushed forward from the lines and threw themselves upon the retreating French.
